raw.description:
The Role

Tolken is a deeply technical team looking for a builder who craves complexity and ownership. You will work across the stack, from the core ledger to the user interface, ensuring systems are not just functional, but hyper-scalable, secure, and auditable. You will be hands-on in design, implementation, and deployment, collaborating closely with the founders to ship production-grade features in a high-velocity environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain end-to-end features across backend (ledger, routing services) and frontend (React-based UI).

  • Implement and evolve production-grade APIs, data models, and integrations for a high-throughput financial system.

  • Own the full lifecycle of features: design, implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing reliability in production.

  • Collaborate closely with the VP of Engineering, founders, and other engineers to translate product requirements into technical designs and delivery plans.

  • Improve performance, scalability, and observability of the platform through profiling, tuning, and better monitoring.

  • Contribute to engineering standards, code reviews, and technical decision-making in a fast-paced startup environment

Stack & Core Requirements

  • 5+ years building high-throughput, distributed backend systems; you understand the difference between “working” and “production-grade.”

  • Strong backend experience in Python (FastAPI preferred), Go, or Java.

  • Strong command of modern frontend stacks (e.g., React) and ability to build complex, data-dense interfaces.

  • Deep understanding of modern database design; depth in Postgres and Redis is a strong plus.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud-native environments (GCP preferred), containers, and Kubernetes.

System Architecture & Practices

  • Mastery of distributed systems concepts: microservices, idempotency, retry/backoff strategies, and eventual consistency.

  • Experience with event-driven architectures and high-volume queues (e.g., Kafka, Redis Streams) and caching layers.

  • You build with observability in mind: metrics, tracing, and logging, and are comfortable working with modern monitoring stacks.

Requirements

Essential:

  • 5+ years of experience as a full stack or backend-heavy engineer working on production systems.

  • Strong proficiency in at least one of: Python (FastAPI preferred), Go, or Java, including building and operating APIs.

  • Solid experience with modern frontend frameworks (e.g., React), comfortable building complex, data-dense interfaces.

  • Strong experience with relational databases and caches; depth in Postgres and Redis is highly valued.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud-native infrastructure (GCP preferred), Docker, and Kubernetes.

  • Solid understanding of distributed systems, event-driven architectures, and designing for reliability and scalability.

  • Comfortable operating in a low-structure, high-ambiguity startup environment with a high degree of ownership.

Desirable:

  • Web3 & privacy: experience with Ethereum/L2s, smart contracts, and especially zero-knowledge proofs (zkSNARKs) for privacy-preserving audit trails.

  • AI/ML: experience with graph-based models, fraud detection, or anomaly detection on live transaction streams.

  • Fintech DNA: background in payments, treasury, or other high-audit, regulated environments.

  • Prior early-stage startup experience and familiarity with rapid iteration and continuous delivery.

Who You Are

  • First-Principles Thinker: You don't just use tools; you understand why they work. You can reason from the ground up to solve novel problems in hybrid (Fiat/Crypto) finance.

  • High Velocity: You move extremely fast and thrive in high-ambiguity environments. You ship to learn.

  • Low Ego, High Output: You care about the product, not the pedigree. You are comfortable switching contexts rapidly—debugging a race condition one hour and designing a new API the next.

  • Owner Mindset: You don't wait for a ticket. You see a gap, you step in, and you fix it.

Equal Opportunities Statement

Tolken is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Please note this posting is to advertise potential job opportunities. This exact role may not be open today but could open in the near future. When you apply, a Cisco representative may contact you directly if a relevant position opens.

This role may be eligible for remote work in the United States depending on business needs and hiring manager approval.

Meet the Team

At Foundation AI, we are leading frontier AI research across Cisco. Our mission is to advance the state of AI. We translate that research into purpose-built models, agentic systems, new algorithms, optimization methods, and scalable data processing techniques that solve real-world problems at scale.

We explore new model architectures, pre-training and post-training methods, inference optimization, evaluation techniques, and data pipelines. Together, we are advancing AI at Cisco and for the broader AI community!


Your Impact

As an AI Researcher, you will work on the research, development, and deployment of advanced AI systems. Your focus will span large language models, agentic AI, multimodal learning, and enterprise-scale AI applications. We are looking for researchers who will help translate frontier research into practical systems by designing experiments, developing new methods, and turning research insights into impactful, scalable AI solutions.

We are particularly interested in researchers with deep expertise in algorithm design for pre-training and post-training, scalable data curation, and reliable AI infrastructure. You will drive improvements to training algorithms, curate and optimize data at scale, and design infrastructure needed to train purpose-built models that can compete with frontier models on specific tasks aligned with Cisco's business priorities and Foundation AI's research agenda.

We place a strong emphasis on publishing research and contributing meaningfully to the AI community. In this role, you will write scientific articles for top-tier machine learning and AI conferences, publish technical blog posts, and contribute to the open-source AI community!

In this role, you will:

  • Develop scalable data curation and processing methods that improve model training and task-specific performance.
  • Build production-ready AI systems using strong software engineering practices.
  • Optimize large language models and agentic systems for enterprise and security-focused use cases.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in one of the following:

-An undergraduate degree program (Associate's or Bachelor's) with 2 years of work experience; or

-A Master’s degree program with 0 years of work experience.

-Qualifying education and work experience should be in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Engineering or a related field. or a related field or a related field.

-Expected to continue enrollment in degree program following completion of the internship.

  • Strong experience with Python, PyTorch, production-grade software engineering practices, and common AI/ML libraries
  • Experience with large language models, model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, inference, and optimization
  • Strong understanding of data pipelines, model experimentation, and scalable AI system design
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain complex research and engineering concepts to cross-functional partners

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing scalable data curation methods and building reliable infrastructure for large-scale model training, evaluation, inference, and deployment
  • Experience deploying high-performance inference engines such as vLLM, NVIDIA Triton, or TorchServe, and working with cloud-native deployment, Docker, Kubernetes, MLOps pipelines, and major cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure
  • Demonstrated history of publishing research in top-tier AI/ML conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or ACL, or contributing to significant open-source AI projects
  • Experience designing and scaling agentic AI workflows, multi-agent frameworks, and autonomous AI systems
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity principles, AI systems for security-focused use cases, safety, and robust machine learning

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

Please see the Cisco careers site to discover more benefits and perks. Employees may be eligible to receive grants of Cisco restricted stock units, which vest following continued employment with Cisco for defined periods of time.

U.S. employees are eligible for paid time away as described below, subject to Cisco’s policies:

For non-quota-based sales performance elements such as strategic sales objectives, Cisco may pay 0% up to 125% of target. Cisco sales plans do not have a minimum threshold of performance for sales incentive compensation to be paid.

Lean 4 Developer

Pay: $60–$120/hour equivalent, paid per accepted task

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor

Time Commitment: 15+ hours per week

Schedule: Flexible

micro1 is looking for developers with practical Lean 4 experience to contribute to a project focused on improving advanced AI systems.

You will use Lean 4 and your software-development or formal-verification expertise to create challenging technical tasks, implement machine-checked reference solutions, evaluate generated code, and establish objective standards for correct solutions.

This opportunity is suited to Lean developers, formal verification engineers, proof-assistant developers, programming-languages researchers, and software engineers working with machine-checked systems. Prior professional AI-training experience is not required.

What You’ll Work On

  1. Create technical tasks involving Lean 4 programming, formal verification, and machine-checked reasoning.
  2. Develop precise specifications, definitions, theorem statements, and reference solutions.
  3. Build self-contained and reproducible Lean projects.
  4. Evaluate generated Lean code for correctness and identify type errors, dependency issues, failed tactics, or incorrect abstractions.

Public Proof of Skill

Strong applicants should provide evidence such as:

  1. Public Lean 4 repositories
  2. Mathlib or Lean ecosystem contributions
  3. Formal verification projects
  4. Lean tactics, libraries, tooling, or metaprogramming projects
  5. Research papers or technical reports involving proof assistants
  6. Open-source programming-language or verification contributions

Please provide your GitHub username and links to your strongest Lean 4 work.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Contributions to mathlib, Lean, or another established Lean project.
  2. Experience building or maintaining substantial Lean codebases.
  3. Experience with Lean metaprogramming, tactic development, or formal verification.

Application Process

  1. Submit your application and describe your Lean 4 development experience.
  2. Provide links to relevant repositories, pull requests, publications, or technical projects.
  3. Complete an AI interview covering Lean development, debugging, and programming.
  4. If experience is relevant, you'll be moved to hiring-manager review.
  5. If selected, complete onboarding and begin your first assigned task.

Compensation

  1. Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid for tasks that meet project specifications and quality requirements. Task availability and completion time may vary.

raw.excerpt: About Darkroom Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow.
raw.description:
About Darkroom

Darkroom is the leading next-generation growth marketing firm engineering the brands of tomorrow. Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom's role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the Role

This role owns Darkroom's creator program and builds Shadow's from nothing. The Darkroom program is run today by the VP of Marketing, which caps how far it can go.

Our creators are operators. They run brands, agencies, and growth teams, and their audiences are founders, marketers, and operators making buying decisions. That makes this a B2B creator role, which is the part we care about most. Sourcing is judged on operating credibility and point of view rather than follower count, and the commercial structure runs closer to a partnership than to a rate card for a sponsored post. Someone whose background is fashion or consumer product influencer campaigns will find that very little of that experience transfers.

The two sides of the job have separate goals. At Darkroom you grow the roster and the volume and quality of what it publishes across Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube. At Shadow you build a creator-led acquisition funnel that does not exist yet, measured on signups rather than on Darkroom's follower numbers. You will report to the VP of Marketing and work alongside a designer, a video editor, and a Marketing Ops & Social Media Manager who keeps the creator CRM current. Design and video are not your job. You brief the designer and video editor for the assets creators need, and you own the relationships and the funnel.

This is a fully remote role supporting a team in the EST time zone, and we are hiring for it in Brazil, Portugal, and Spain.

What You'll Do

Darkroom's Creator Program

  • Run the existing roster day to day: relationships, briefs, scheduling, and the cadence of what they publish.

  • Source new operator-creators, judged on what they have built and how sharp their thinking is.

  • Raise the volume and quality of creator content across Instagram, LinkedIn, X, and YouTube, working toward the Instagram target of 40,000 followers by the end of 2027.

  • Collect and organize reviews, testimonials, and social proof from creators and clients so the rest of the team can use them.

Shadow's Creator Channel

  • Build the channel from zero: find the operators whose audiences are Shadow's buyers, and bring them on.

  • Design a creator-led acquisition funnel, from post to signup, and work with the Retention Marketer on the email path behind it.

  • Report on it as its own channel, measured on signups and pipeline rather than folded into Darkroom's numbers.

Across Both

  • Structure and manage the commercial side of each relationship: fees, affiliate and referral terms, co-marketing, advisory arrangements.

  • Feed creators the strategy, data, and product access they need to say something specific rather than generic.

  • Keep the creator CRM accurate, working with the Marketing Ops Manager.

  • Know which creators are producing results and which are not, and act on it.

What We're Looking For

  • A real understanding of B2B. This is the most important thing on this list. Our creators talk to founders, operators, and growth teams, and a creator program run like a consumer brand's will not work here.

  • Genuine experience running creator, partner, or community programs where the creators were practitioners with an audience. Years matter less than whether you have actually done it.

  • Enough commerce and growth literacy to hold a real conversation with someone who runs a brand or an agency. Creators at this level work out within one exchange whether you know the space.

  • Smart in a way that shows up in the work. You can judge whether an audience is real, structure a deal that works for both sides, and brief someone without flattening their voice.

  • Experience structuring the commercial side of these relationships, including fees, affiliate and referral terms, and co-marketing.

  • Organized enough to run a growing roster without anything slipping: contracts, deliverables, payment schedules, all of it.

  • AI-native. Our team works alongside AI for analytics, reporting, and drafting, and you should be excited to build workflows with it.

  • Comfortable building a channel that does not exist yet, for Shadow, while running an established one, for Darkroom, at the same time.

Bonus Points

  • You have built an audience of your own, on any platform.

  • Experience marketing a SaaS or software product to a business audience.

  • Agency, ecommerce, or performance marketing background.

  • You already know creators in the commerce, growth, or B2B software space.

  • Familiarity with Notion, our operating layer.

Working at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership — but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape — just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + Local holidays (Relevant to your hub): Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Remote-First Culture: Many roles are fully remote. Employees based in or near our New York or Lisbon HQs are expected to work hybrid with weekly in-office time. Hub locations include the Brazil and Spain.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national orientation, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week

Please note that eligibility may vary depending on your location, as some regions may not be supported by the client.

Check out this Loom video for more details:

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.

What this role actually is

You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:

• Whether the response makes sense

  • Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
  • Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
  • Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer

This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.

What you'll be doing

  • Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
  • Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
  • Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
  • Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
  • Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
  • Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code

What we mean by "taste"

We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:

  • Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
  • Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
  • Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
  • Would this interaction build or erode trust?

You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.

Who you are

  • Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
  • Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
  • Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
  • Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
  • Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
  • High bar for what good engineering looks like

Nice to have

  • Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
  • Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards

Engagement details

  • Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location

• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible

  • Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
  • Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
  • Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

Revenue manager for a shared portfolio of Hyatt hotels in Mexico, translating demand, market, and performance data into coordinated pricing, inventory, distribution, and forecasting decisions. The Revenue Manager partners with each General Manager and hotel commercial team to grow rooms revenue and market share while maintaining alignment with Hyatt standards and property-specific business needs. The initial portfolio comprises Hyatt Centric Playa del Carmen and Hyatt Regency Villahermosa.

Key Responsibilities

1. Develop and execute property-specific revenue strategies across transient, group, negotiated, wholesale, and other applicable segments, balancing rate, occupancy, channel mix, and total rooms revenue.

2.Use Hyatt revenue management systems, including Ideas, as a core part of daily analysis and decision-making. Review system recommendations, demand signals, pace, pickup, booking patterns, restrictions, and forecasts; apply informed judgment and document material overrides.

3.Manage pricing and inventory across direct, GDS, OTA, wholesale, and other distribution channels. Maintain rate and room-type integrity, monitor parity and channel performance, and recommend promotions and visibility actions based on need periods and return.

4.Own the portfolio revenue forecast process in line with Hyatt timelines and standards, including short-term and monthly outlooks. Explain material variances, risks, and opportunities to hotel leaders and regional stakeholders.

5.Support each property’s annual budget through demand analysis, assumptions, scenarios, and feedback. The property team retains ownership of preparing and approving its budget.

6.Lead or contribute to regular commercial strategy and revenue meetings for each assigned hotel. Review current performance, future demand, group displacement and pricing, need periods, business mix, and clear actions with accountable owners.

7.Provide Daily Business Review (DBR) analysis and recommendations using the applicable Hyatt process. Share concise, timely updates with hotel teams and escalate material changes in demand or performance.

8.Partner with Sales, Marketing, Reservations, Front Office, and other revenue-generating departments to align account strategy, group opportunities, campaigns, upsell opportunities, and inventory decisions with each hotel’s goals.

9.Monitor market conditions, competitor pricing, events, and economic or travel trends in each destination. Translate findings into practical decisions and communicate implications to the relevant hotel teams.

10.Build proactive relationships with hotel leadership and owners, presenting performance, risks, opportunities, and revenue recommendations in a clear, evidence-based manner.

11.Coordinate support across the shared portfolio by setting a consistent operating rhythm, prioritizing time against business need, maintaining reliable handoffs, and documenting decisions so coverage continues during absences or peak workload.

12.Maintain accurate system setup and data quality across assigned revenue tools and distribution platforms. Follow Hyatt Revenue Management standards, controls, and procedures; protect confidential business information.

Measures of Success

1.Rooms revenue and market share performance against budget, forecast, and relevant competitive benchmarks.

2.Forecast accuracy and timely completion of required reporting and revenue processes.

3.Quality and business impact of pricing, inventory, segment, and distribution decisions.

4.Effective execution of Hyatt revenue standards and use of Ideas and other required systems.

5.Hotel stakeholder confidence, clear communication, and consistent coverage across the assigned portfolio.

Working Relationships

Works closely with the General Managers and hotel commercial teams at each assigned property, including Sales, Marketing, Reservations, and Operations and collaborates with regional revenue resources.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in hospitality, business, finance, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
  • At least three years of hotel revenue management experience preferred, with demonstrated responsibility for pricing, forecasting, inventory, and distribution.
  • Experience supporting multiple hotels or working across more than one market is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, financial, planning, and problem-solving skills; able to interpret hotel performance reports and communicate clear recommendations.
  • Professional proficiency in English and Spanish preferred for effective collaboration across the assigned hotels and regional teams.

Systems and Technical Skills

  • Required: working proficiency with Hyatt Revenue Management Systems (Ideas) Hyatt PrO, Optix and RevPlan, including use of system insight tools such as STR, Amadeus BI and Lighthouse to inform pricing, inventory, and forecasting decisions.
  • Experience with hotel property management, central reservation, distribution, and business intelligence tools preferred, including Opera, Hyatt CRS (Reserve), SynXis as applicable.
  • Strong Microsoft Excel skills and working proficiency with Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

Core Competencies

  • Sound commercial judgment and comfort making timely decisions with incomplete or changing information.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise performance summaries and presentations.
  • Collaboration, organization, adaptability, and the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple properties.

Compensation and Role Parameters

  • The position is eligible for the applicable Revenue Management compensation plan.

Work Conditions

The role is primarily remote and requires extended computer use, virtual collaboration, and periodic in-person engagement at assigned properties. Travel toproperties may be required based on business needs. The employee must be able to communicate effectively, review detailed information on screen, and move through hotel work areas as needed.

raw.description:
C++ Software Engineer

Remote (UK-based) | Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

We're looking for a C++ Software Engineer who wants to build low-latency trading infrastructure on Linux. You'll work on the core components of our Switchboard trading platform — pricing engines, connectivity gateways, market-data systems, and the messaging layer that ties them together.

This is not a role where you write code and throw it over a wall. You build it, you test it, you deploy it, you support it in production, and you improve it. Our engineers own the full lifecycle — from design through to operational excellence. When something breaks at 4pm on a Friday, you're part of the team that investigates and fixes it.

Occasional hours outside the normal working day are required for production releases, scheduled maintenance windows, and Level 3 support during critical incidents. We keep this to a minimum and recognise the commitment — but owning a production trading platform means being there when it matters.

What You'll Work On

  • Modern C++20 and Go on Linux — a modern software stack based on open source

  • Cloud-native infrastructure on AWS with colocation in key data centres

  • Microsecond-level latency optimisation and high-throughput messaging

  • Market-data and reference-data pipelines across multiple asset classes

  • FIX protocol integrations with global banks and liquidity providers

  • Observability and monitoring — dashboards, alerting, and metrics that make system behaviour visible

  • Production systems that handle real money — reliability is not optional

What We Need

Technical:

  • Strong C++ with Linux systems programming (3+ years)

  • Comfortable working close to the metal — you understand what's underneath your code

  • Experience with performance-sensitive systems (profiling, optimisation, deterministic behaviour)

  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals (TCP/UDP, socket programming)

  • Go experience is a strong bonus — we use Go extensively for microservices and command-line tooling, and you'll be expected to work with it internally. If you don't know it yet, strong C++ engineers pick it up quickly

  • Python for scripting, automation, testing, and data analysis — used across the platform for tooling and operational workflows

  • Git and shell scripting

  • Experience in financial services or trading technology is a plus but not essential

How you work:

  • You ship. You're delivery-focused — you iterate, you improve, you get things into production

  • You own it. When you build something, you take responsibility for its behaviour in production. You respond to incidents (15-minute acknowledgement SLA during working hours), investigate issues, and close the loop

  • You write things down. Documentation is not an afterthought — it's how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You communicate. We're a distributed team across multiple time zones. Clear, proactive communication — especially when things go wrong — is essential

  • You care about quality. You write clean, testable code. You review your peers' work thoughtfully. You push for continuous improvement without gold-plating

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools (Claude, Gemini) to amplify our engineering capability — from code review and debugging to incident investigation and documentation. You don't need to be an expert, but you should be curious and willing to learn

What You Get

  • Real problems —trading systems where performance is measured in microseconds, not user clicks

  • An excellent team — senior engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

  • Competitive package — up to 30 days leave + bank holidays, private health insurance, pension, life insurance, dental/optical cashback, cycle to work, socials and offsites

  • Remote-friendly — work from home with flexibility. We trust our people to deliver

  • Sustainable pace — we work hard, but we don't burn people out. Balance is how we stay sharp

  • Growth — career progression to senior roles, performance specialisation, or technical leadership. We invest in people who invest in us

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition

Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager

Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the UK. We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

  • Identify and anticipate operational and quality risks, proactively escalate issues, and drive timely resolution with the Study Management Team

  • Develop and maintain study management plans, timelines, risk assessments, and operational documentation
  • Ensure consistent use of study tools, training materials, and compliance with SOPs, policies, and procedures

Required qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience independently leading primary data collection observational studies from startup through closeout
  • Experience implementing patient-reported outcomes within primary data collection studies
  • Strong knowledge of observational research and RWE study execution, including the operational differences between clinical trials and observational studies
  • Experience working across both primary and secondary data real-world study designs
  • Virology experience strongly preferred
  • Knowledge of ICH GCP and relevant local laws, regulations, and guidelines applicable to clinical and observational research
  • Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to handle conflicting priorities
  • Ability to work effectively across geographies and cultures
  • Ability to demonstrate all IQVIA core competencies (Ownership, Innovation, Collaboration, Growth)

raw.description:
Operations Engineer

Hybrid or Remote (UK-based), Hybrid or Remote (US-based) Full-Time

About Us

Reactive Markets is the 2026 OTC Trading Platform of the Year (). Our network handles over $75 billion in daily trading volumes across FX, Equities, and Cryptocurrency, connecting 60+ of the world's leading liquidity providers.

We build trading systems that operate at the edge of what's technically possible — where nanoseconds matter and a dropped message costs real money. Our engineering team is small, senior, and deeply invested in the craft of building cutting edge, reliable, high-performance systems.

The Role

As an Operations Engineer, you will ensure the stability, performance, and availability of the Reactive trading platform. This is a hands-on, technical operations role — focused on production systems, infrastructure, and trading workflows rather than client relationship management.

You'll work closely with Engineering, Product, and internal stakeholders as the first line of defence for live trading systems. TechOps owns Level 1 and Level 2 support — monitoring response and alert triage through to the deeper technical investigation, configuration delivery, and post-release verification that sits beneath it — escalating to Level 3 (Engineering and Infrastructure) only when an issue genuinely requires code changes or deep infrastructure intervention. While the role involves supporting client onboarding and integrations, the emphasis is on technical delivery, system correctness, and incident response — not sales or account management.

Reactive runs a globally distributed, follow-the-sun operations team, and we are hiring across our UK, US, and Singapore hubs. You'll provide operational coverage across your regional trading session — the eyes on the platform when your region is live — and hand over cleanly to the next hub as the day moves. In each region you own the full TechOps remit: monitoring and incident response through the session, plus the configuration delivery, onboarding execution, and change work that keeps the platform growing. The UK and US roles are remote; the Singapore role is office-based.

We are a small team that has turned operations into a genuine engineering discipline, and we are investing heavily in AI-assisted tooling and knowledge engineering to keep it that way. This role suits someone with experience in trading or FinTech operations who enjoys working close to production systems, solving complex problems, writing things down properly, and taking ownership in a fast-moving environment.

What You'll Work On

Production Monitoring & Incident Response:

  • Monitor live trading systems across multiple regions, venues, and asset classes — you are the eyes on the platform during the trading session

  • Own Level 1 and Level 2 response: triage alerts, run standard runbook actions (restart, rollback, failover, feature flag), investigate deeply, declare severity, and coordinate incidents — escalating to Level 3 (Engineering / Infrastructure) only when code or deep infrastructure intervention is genuinely required

  • Participate in failover and disaster-recovery readiness — rehearsed, playbook-driven, and time-bound

  • Drive root-cause analysis and blameless post-incident reviews, turning every incident into a runbook or a tooling improvement

Configuration Delivery & Production Change:

  • Deliver the production-change pipeline that brings new clients, liquidity providers, venues, and capabilities live — the largest share of the work

  • Configure and maintain FIX sessions by function — streaming, RFQ, algo, and post-trade — alongside cross-rates, indications of interest, subscriptions, certificate rotations, and pool registrations

  • Execute changes safely against the platform's deployment configuration, with schema updates, ACL coordination, and post-release verification

  • Support migrations, decommissioning, and the follow-on work that keeps the production estate coherent as it grows

Client Onboarding & Connectivity:

  • Own the technical execution of client and LP onboarding: credentials, IPs, conformance and UAT testing, cross-connects, day-1 readiness, and post-go-live verification

  • Act as the technical point of contact during onboarding, giving Client Services the information they need to manage the relationship

  • Monitor and validate FIX message flows, identifying issues related to execution, routing, or market-data

  • Maintain clear, accurate documentation for configurations, onboarding steps, and troubleshooting

Knowledge Engineering, Automation & Continuous Improvement:

  • Contribute to capacity and infrastructure planning — session load balancing, gateway placement, and utilisation monitoring — jointly with Performance Engineering and Infrastructure

  • Coordinate with external vendors and counterparties: network and colocation providers, post-trade vendors, and liquidity providers and their infrastructure teams

  • Identify recurring issues and contribute to long-term fixes and preventative improvements

  • Help build operational tooling, automation, runbooks, and the knowledge corpus — including AI-assisted investigation and documentation — that reduce toil and make the platform less dependent on individual memory

What We Need

Technical:

  • 2+ years' experience in operations or production support within trading or FinTech

  • Working knowledge of the FIX protocol, ideally in FX or electronic trading environments

  • Understanding of trading infrastructure, networking, and low-latency connectivity

  • Experience with monitoring and alerting tools in live production environments

  • Linux fundamentals — our platform runs on Linux throughout

  • Comfortable with configuration-as-code — Git, structured config (YAML), and making changes that are reviewed, version-controlled, and verified before they reach production

  • Scripting and automation (e.g. Bash, Python) — used daily to investigate, automate, and reduce toil; you don't need to be a software engineer, but you should be able to read and write working scripts

How you work:

  • You own it. When a production issue lands, you take responsibility — you investigate, you escalate when needed, you close the loop. You don't wait to be told

  • You stay calm under pressure. Trading systems don't pause for debugging. You can think clearly, prioritise effectively, and communicate status when things go wrong

  • You write things down. Runbooks, configuration notes, post-incident reviews — documentation is how we scale knowledge across a distributed team. If it's not written down, it doesn't exist

  • You communicate. Clear, proactive communication with engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike. When something breaks, people need to know what's happening and what you're doing about it

  • You improve things. You spot recurring problems and fix them properly — automation, better tooling, clearer processes. You don't just fight the same fires repeatedly

  • You embrace AI tooling. We use AI tools to amplify our operational capability — from incident investigation to documentation. You should be curious and willing to learn, and comfortable helping build the corpus that makes those tools better

What You Get

  • Real systems — a market-leading trading platform with genuine scale and technical depth

  • Breadth — exposure to multiple asset classes, LP integrations, and global trading infrastructure

  • A genuinely technical Ops role — this is engineering-led operations with ownership and impact, not ticket-shuffling

  • An excellent team — experienced engineers who care about craft, collaborate openly, and hold each other to high standards

  • Ownership — small teams, clear accountability, direct impact on the platform and our clients

  • Competitive package — competitive compensation and benefits aligned to your local market

  • Flexible working — remote-friendly in the UK and US; office-based and collaborative in Singapore. We trust our people to deliver

  • Growth — as the platform scales, so does the opportunity. Operations engineers who understand the full system are invaluable

We believe in transparency, honest feedback, and writing things down. We celebrate delivery, not activity. We frame AI as empowering people — removing toil, amplifying capability, enabling higher-value work.

We aim to build systems that don't depend on the heroics of individuals to maintain and support — systems and processes that are resilient, documented, and sustainable.

Our Hiring Process

We keep our process focused and respectful of your time. Our process follows three stages.

Stage 1: Initial Conversation with Talent Acquisition

Format: Video call, ~30-45 minutes

Stage 2: Hiring Manager Conversation with the relevant team lead or hiring manager

Format: Video call, ~60 minutes

Stage 3: Technical Interview with two members of the relevant engineering team
Format: Video call, interactive session, ~60 minutes

What to expect in each stage will be explained by Talent Acquisition if you're invited to interview. Throughout the process, we aim to keep momentum with no unnecessary delays between stages, and feedback typically comes within a few business days.

*Please note that depending on availability, Stage 2 and 3 may swap around.

How to Apply

Please apply directly via this job posting — all applications, including those submitted via LinkedIn, are managed through our applicant tracking system, so you'll always land in the same place regardless of where you found this role.

Right to Work: Candidates must have the existing right to work in the country associated with the location advertised for this role (UK, US, or Singapore, as applicable). We are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship for this role in any location.

Equal Opportunities: Reactive Markets is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation.

Reasonable Adjustments: If you need any adjustments or support during the application or interview process, please let us know — we're happy to accommodate.

Data Protection: By applying, you consent to Reactive Markets processing your personal data for recruitment purposes, in line with our privacy policy.

raw.description:
Peek is the operating system powering the experiences industry - from museums and attractions to tours and activities. With over $7B in bookings, Peek’s AI-powered platform has helped thousands of merchants to increase revenues, save time, and deliver seamless guest experiences. Customers include MoMA, Whitney Museum, Seattle Aquarium, Bryant Park & Looping Group. The company has raised over $150 million from institutional investors Westcap, Goldman Sachs, and SpringCoast Partners. Learn more at .

As a remote-first company recognized by Forbes as one of America's Best Startup Employers and by Built In as a 2025 and 2026 Best Place to Work, we are a global team of "Peeksters" who "Obsess Over Our Customers," "Accomplish Big Things," "Collaborate With Purpose," and "Get Better Every Day.

We're looking for a hands-on DevSecOps Engineer to embed security into our infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud environment. You'll own the technical controls and evidence that keep us PCI DSS 4.0 and SOC 2 Type II compliant, drive vulnerability remediation across our container and VM fleet, and build out the disaster recovery testing program. This is a role for someone who's comfortable moving between hands-on technical remediation, audit-facing documentation, and cross-functional work with engineering, IT, and procurement.

Our team is 100% remote, however, we prefer candidates in the same time zones as the greater United States (UTC-10 to UTC-4).

We will occasionally require you to work outside of normal business hours on infrastructure upgrades and maintenance. We are committed to working with you to keep a healthy and balanced schedule.

About the Team

We’re a small DevOps team supporting the whole Engineering organization, building applications on top of GCP and AWS. We own all aspects of the SDLC but strive to automate self-service wherever possible. Being a small team, we also practice SRE, continuously improving our observability and building with Infrastructure-as-Code. Security and compliance best practices are integral to our workflows, ensuring systems are secure by design and meet regulatory and organizational standards. Our team is remote but highly organized to meet the demand of a fast-paced environment. Our primary business language is English, and we emphasize strong communication skills.

About You

You're a security-minded engineer who's as comfortable in a Kubernetes cluster or CI/CD pipeline as you are explaining a control to an auditor. You own remediation end to end, like automating away repetitive security work, and are energized by helping a growing company scale security without slowing the business down.

What You'll Do

  • Own technical security controls across GCP and AWS: least-privilege IAM and RBAC, WAF, container and image security, and secure CI/CD.

  • Drive vulnerability remediation end to end: triage, prioritize, and automate fixes, partnering with the rest of the DevOps team on production rollout.

  • Build automated scanning and remediation into our pipelines.

  • Tune WAF policies and the OWASP Core Rule Set to protect public-facing applications without blocking legitimate traffic.

  • Run PCI DSS vulnerability scanning, including quarterly external ASV scans, and drive remediation of findings.

  • Contribute to incident response planning and exercises, and ensure backups and recovery processes meet security requirements for encryption, access, and integrity.

  • Produce and automate evidence for technical controls, and keep our cloud environments connected to our compliance platform (Drata).

  • Serve as technical expert for audits, customer security reviews, and vendor assessments involving sensitive data.

Requirements

  • 3+ years in DevSecOps, security engineering, cloud security, or a closely related role

  • Hands-on experience securing GCP and/or AWS, including managed Kubernetes (GKE, EKS)

  • Container and vulnerability management, including building automated remediation (tools such as Trivy, AWS Inspector, Amazon ECR scanning, GCP Artifact Analysis, ZAP)

  • WAF configuration and OWASP Core Rule Set tuning (Cloud Armor, AWS WAF, Cloudflare, or similar)

  • Least-privilege access management across cloud services (IAM, RBAC)

  • Working Linux knowledge sufficient to remediate OS and package vulnerabilities in VMs and container images

  • Scripting in Python, Bash, or similar

  • CI/CD experience (GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Codefresh, or similar)

  • Experience working in a PCI DSS or SOC 2 environment, including producing evidence for technical controls

  • Clear written communication with both technical and non-technical audiences

Nice to Haves

  • Low-downtime patching approaches (rolling updates, blue/green, live patching such as kpatch or Livepatch)

  • PCI ASV scanning with Tenable or a comparable platform

  • Drata or a similar compliance automation platform

  • Serverless platforms (Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, AWS Lambda)

  • Cloud security posture tools such as ScoutSuite or Mondoo

  • Contributing to third-party risk reviews involving PII

  • Agentic or AI-assisted penetration testing

  • Certifications such as OSCP, CISSP, CISM, or AWS/GCP Security Specialty

Peek Travel Inc. is an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

If you are unable to apply due to incompatible assistive technology or a disability, please contact us at . We will make every effort to respond to your request for disability assistance as soon as possible.

raw.description:
Type: Full-time, 40 hours a week, contract, month to month

Location: Remote, any country. You must work US Eastern hours.

Pay: $5,000 to $10,000 a month (USD), based on experience, plus 3% of spend on your winning ads

Write the ads that find the next 10,000 bourbon drinkers

Most people who love bourbon have the same problem: they walk into their local liquor store and see the same 20 bottles every time. The good stuff from small craft distilleries never makes it to the shelf.

Whiskey Library fixes that. Members take a 90-second palate quiz and get a monthly Bourbon Mystery Box of full-size bottles, picked from hundreds of craft distilleries, including single barrel picks you can't buy anywhere else. We grew from $2,500 into an eight-figure subscription business with over 10,000 members, and we spend over $15,000 a day on Meta.

Every dollar of that spend runs on creative. This is the seat that decides what we say.

Why this role

  • You own creative strategy. You work directly with the CMO, not inside a big agency hierarchy.
  • A real team behind you. Editors, UGC creators and AI tools turn your briefs into finished ads.
  • A path up. This seat grows into leading the creative team as spend scales.
  • Real mentorship. Weekly reviews of every ad's result: what worked, why, and what we test next.

What you'll do

  • Start with the customer, not the product. Dig into reviews, survey answers, support tickets, comments and competitor ads. Open every ad on the customer's problem, in the customer's words.
  • Find new angles. Turn that research into concepts, each built on one angle, one avatar and one clear reason to believe.
  • Write the hooks and scripts. Make the first 3 seconds stop a bourbon drinker's scroll.
  • Brief editors and creators so well they need no follow-up call. Then review their work until it's ready to launch.
  • Iterate on winners the right way. When an ad works, protect it. Build new ads that test one named change at a time instead of breaking what's working.
  • Run the learnings. Label every ad's result, say why it won or lost, and feed that into the next brief.
  • Use AI as your production engine. Claude, Claude Code and AI image and video tools for research, scripts and variations. You still bring the ideas.

What we're looking for

  • You've written direct response ads that ran on Meta, and you can show them. Spend, CPA or sales on the ads you wrote are a big plus.
  • You think in business results, not output. "This ad took 30% of spend at our target CPA" beats "I shipped 40 concepts."
  • You close the loop. You can tell us what an ad taught you, how you applied it, and what changed.
  • You already use AI in your work, and you're comfortable getting your hands dirty with tools like Claude Code. We don't hire people who won't use AI.
  • You own your work. You get things done without being asked, deliver briefs on time, communicate clearly and ask good questions.
  • You move fast and care. We're a small team in a fast-paced environment.
  • Nice to have: subscription, food and beverage or spirits experience.

How we measure success

  • Share of ad spend going to ads you created
  • Concepts and briefs delivered each week, with intent behind each one
  • How your ads perform against our targets

Pay and structure

  • $5,000 to $10,000 a month, contract, month to month, 40 hours a week, based on experience. The top of the range is for a strategist with proven winners who can lead the team.
  • Bonus: 3% of the monthly ad spend on ads you created that hit our target cost per order. Example: if your ads spend $50,000 in a month at target, you earn $1,500 on top of base. Paid monthly, no cap.
  • Growth path to leading the creative team as spend scales

How hiring works

1. Apply with your portfolio, three short answers and a short hook test (below).

2. First call (30 minutes): a working session on your past ads. Be ready to show us the real results of ads you wrote. What did you learn, how did you apply it, what changed?

3. Paid test: $250 flat, 48 hours, capped at 4 hours. Tear down our live Whiskey Library ads: the top problems you see and how you'd fix them, plus a few new hooks. Paid whether or not you're hired.

4. Final call with the CMO: we walk through your test together and you defend your choices. We'll ask to speak with one past employer.

5. Paid 30-day trial at your full monthly rate, with daily contact and a weekly check-in. Written decision at day 30.

We hire off the test and the trial, not the interview.

How to apply (required)

1. Apply on this page.

2. Add a link to your portfolio: ads you wrote that ran as paid social. Your portfolio is all we need to see. Do not send separate sample files.

3. Answer three short questions:

  • Pick one ad you wrote that worked. Why did it work, and what did you test next?
  • Tell us about an ad that lost. What did it teach you, and how did you use that?
  • Walk us through how you use AI in your creative work, step by step.

4. Hook test: Write 3 hooks for a 15-second Meta ad for our Bourbon Mystery Box. The viewer is a bourbon drinker who keeps buying the same bottles because he can't find anything new at his local store. One line each, the first words someone hears or reads. Write them yourself, no AI.

Applications without a portfolio link are not reviewed.

  • Drive developer delight and operational efficiency through automation, self-service tooling, and streamlined workflows for deploying and managing API gateways, while proactively preventing technical debt and reducing operational toil.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, engineering, and support teams to influence roadmap decisions and ensure operational readiness for new features.

What You'll Bring:

The Toolkit

  • Proven experience leading and managing Site Reliability Engineering or DevOps teams in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

  • Deep expertise in designing, deploying, and operating highly available distributed systems on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).

  • Extensive hands-on experience with Kubernetes (k8s) and container orchestration in production environments.

  • Proficiency in Golang or similar modern programming languages for infrastructure automation and service development.

  • Strong understanding of observability principles and experience with tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar.

  • Demonstrated ability to manage critical incidents, perform root cause analysis, and implement effective preventative measures.

  • Familiarity with API gateway technologies, service mesh, or network proxies is a significant plus.

The Kong DNA

  • Ownership: You take full responsibility for the reliability and performance of systems, driving initiatives from conception to completion.

  • Urgency: You thrive in dynamic environments, prioritizing critical issues and delivering impactful solutions with speed and precision.

  • Experience with open-source contributions or active participation in SRE/cloud-native communities.

The role

Syd is looking for an AI Research Engineer to join the AI & Research team and work directly with the team lead on open problems across the full range of Syd's work , from the intelligence members interact with to the models , data and research systems behind it . AI tools write most of the code in our team , and you will use them every day . Your contribution is the question you ask , the experiment you design , the measurement you trust and the decision you can defend . Autonomy is high : you choose problems and propose ideas , with direction and review from the team lead .

What you bring

  • A PhD in a quantitative or life science field , such as neuroscience , mathematics , physics , biomedical engineering , statistics or computational biology , or an equivalent record of original research that is active and recent .

  • First-hand work with real , imperfect data , and confidence with study design , effect sizes , uncertainty , baselines and calibration .

  • A first-principles understanding of how large language models are trained and adapted ( pre-training , SFT , LoRA , distillation , PPO and GRPO ) , with hands-on practice in at least one .

  • Evidence discipline : you state what result would prove you wrong before you run the experiment , and report negative results as readily as positive ones .

  • Daily use of coding agents and frontier models , with a clear way of checking their output .

  • Clear , concise written English and comfort working autonomously in a remote team .

What you will do

  • Design new behaviours , memory and tools for language model agents that support members across every dimension of their life quality .

  • Design evaluations before a feature is built , with automated judges validated against human review .

  • Build methods that turn the scientific literature into structured , source-checked evidence .

  • Train predictive models on large real-world datasets , with attention to calibration , bias and validity across populations .

  • Fine-tune and evaluate open and closed models where a specialised model serves people well .

Terms

Remote , open to candidates anywhere in the world . Consulting agreement with equity .

How to apply

Apply at careers.syd.life/careers/ai-research-engineer , with a research sample and a one-page note as described on the page . Every candidate completes an online assessment and a 48-hour task before any interview .

Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

Senior SRE, Managed Gateways

About the Role:

Kong's Managed Gateways is the fastest-growing product in the Kong portfolio, a SaaS offering with ARR growing multifold. As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer focused on Managed Gateways, you'll be instrumental in architecting and maintaining the resilient, scalable infrastructure that powers Kong's mission-critical managed services — and you'll be the technical face of that product for the enterprise customers who depend on it, directly ensuring the reliability and performance that lets them build the next generation of connected applications at global scale.

What You’ll Do:

Cloud Gateways is a complex, multi-cloud problem — supported across AWS, GCP, and Azure — and our enterprise customers run large, often unique topologies. This role carries two equally deep engineering mandates: owning production reliability for the platform, and acting as the senior technical authority who takes an enterprise customer from kickoff to a fully successful, live implementation.

Platform & Reliability Engineering

  • Lead, mentor, and inspire a high-performing team of Site Reliability Engineers dedicated to Kong's Managed Gateway offerings.

  • Architect and implement robust, scalable, and fault-tolerant cloud-native systems using technologies like Kubernetes, Golang, and major cloud providers.

  • Own the end-to-end operational lifecycle, from proactive monitoring and alerting to incident response and blameless post-mortems, ensuring continuous service improvement.

  • Drive a culture of developer delight by implementing automation, self-service tooling, and streamlined workflows for deploying and managing API gateways.

  • Define, track, and report on key SLOs and SLIs to ensure optimal performance and reliability of Managed Gateways.

  • Champion technical debt prevention and advocate for architectural best practices that enhance system resilience and reduce operational toil.

  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Product, engineering, and Customer Success to influence roadmap decisions and ensure operational readiness for new features.

Enterprise Implementation Engineering

  • Partner directly with enterprise customers — working alongside Product leadership, Professional Services, and Customer Success — to drive end-to-end onboarding and implementation of Cloud Gateways, and productize recurring implementation patterns into repeatable playbooks and platform capabilities.

  • Bring deep, cross-cloud breadth (AWS, GCP, Azure) to handle unique customer topologies and turn complex setups into successful, production-ready deployments.

  • Serve as the technical owner of the customer relationship through implementation, primarily supporting our North America customer base, and be the escalation point Customer Success leans on for technically complex accounts.

  • Feed real-world implementation patterns and customer constraints back to Product to further contribute the roadmap.

What You’ll Bring:

The Toolkit

  • Extensive experience as a Site Reliability Engineer, focusing on highly available and distributed systems.

  • Deep expertise with Kubernetes and cloud-native architectures, preferably across multiple public cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).

  • Strong proficiency in Golang or similar modern programming languages for automation and tool development.

  • Proven track record in building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible).

  • In-depth knowledge of monitoring, logging, and alerting systems (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack, Datadog).

  • Experience with managed services, API gateways, or similar network infrastructure is highly desirable.

The Kong DNA

  • You take immense ownership of your systems, treating reliability as a first-class feature.

  • You operate with a sense of urgency, especially in critical situations, and drive quick, effective resolutions.

  • You thrive in a collaborative environment, actively sharing knowledge and elevating the entire team.

  • Kong moves fast, and our team's spread across continents and time zones — plans shift mid-flight, and things don't always line up neatly. You don't need everything settled to do good work. You bring your own calm to the noise, figure things out as you go, and help the people around you do the same.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience with Service Mesh technologies (e.g., Istio, Linkerd).

  • Familiarity with database administration for high-throughput systems (PostgreSQL, Cassandra).

  • Contributions to open-source SRE tools or projects.

  • Relevant cloud certifications (e.g., AWS Certified DevOps Engineer, CKA).

About Kong:

Kong Inc., the AI Connectivity Company, is building the connectivity layer of AI. Trusted by the Fortune 500® and AI-native startups alike, Kong’s unified API and AI platform enables organizations to secure, manage, accelerate, govern, and monetize the flow of intelligence across APIs and AI traffic — on any model, any cloud. For more information, visit .

Compensation Range: $165K - $185K

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for Android engineers to build the native Android experience for BJAK's Android Software Engineer.

This role is for someone who cares about clean user flows, fast performance, product quality and shipping reliable mobile features used by real customers.

What You'll Own

  • Build and ship Android features using Kotlin.

  • 3+ years of Android development experience using Kotlin.

  • Strong Android fundamentals and experience shipping production apps.

  • Good knowledge of Jetpack, Coroutines, Flow and modern Android architecture.

  • Strong sense of mobile UX, usability, edge cases and user flows.

Tech Stack

  • Kotlin

  • Android SDK

The Kind of Builder We Want

Join a global Contract Resource Organization (CRO) where innovation meets purpose. At Worldwide Clinical Trials, we're driven by a shared commitment to improving lives through high-quality clinical research. Our teams are empowered to think creatively, take ownership, and deliver meaningful work that helps bring life-changing therapies to patients around the world.


With more than 4,000 professionals across the globe, we foster a collaborative and inclusive environment where diverse perspectives are valued, growth is encouraged, and every contribution makes an impact. Whether you're building your career or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to learn, grow, and help shape the future of clinical research.


Make an Impact as a Medical Director, Medical Affairs - Neurology at Worldwide


As a Medical Director, Medical Affairs - Neurology, you'll play a critical role in advancing clinical research programs by providing medical leadership, scientific expertise, and oversight throughout the clinical trial lifecycle. Your work will help ensure studies are conducted with the highest standards of patient safety, scientific integrity, and regulatory compliance.


In this role, you'll serve as a Medical Monitor and trusted medical partner to cross-functional teams, investigators, and sponsors. From protocol development and safety review to study execution and scientific communications, you'll have the opportunity to influence key decisions that support successful clinical research outcomes.


You'll also contribute strategic medical insight to business development activities, clinical development planning, and research initiatives, helping drive both program success and organizational growth within the neurology therapeutic area.


Where You'll Work

This is a REMOTE role open to candidates based in US. You will collaborate with global teams across multiple time zones.


What You'll Do

  • Provide medical oversight for assigned clinical trials, serving as the Medical Monitor and guiding medical decision-making throughout study execution.
  • Lead global and pan-regional studies as the Global Lead Medical Monitor, partnering with cross-functional teams to support successful trial delivery.
  • Review serious adverse events (SAEs) and contribute to clinical safety assessments to help protect patient well-being and study integrity.
  • Deliver therapeutic area and protocol-specific training to study teams, promoting strong scientific and clinical understanding across projects.
  • Contribute medical expertise to clinical development programs, study protocols, scientific publications, clinical study reports, and other research documentation.
  • Support business development efforts through feasibility assessments, proposal development, sponsor interactions, and medical services review.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to provide medical guidance, strengthen study quality, and enhance client satisfaction.
  • Maintain deep expertise in neurology and clinical research through ongoing review of scientific literature, professional development, and industry engagement.
  • Mentor medical colleagues and promote high standards of professionalism, ethics, and scientific excellence.


What You'll Bring

  • Medical Degree from an accredited institution of medical education with at least 2 years of medical monitoring experience in clinical research or a related industry environment.
  • Strong knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), clinical development processes, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Experience reviewing, evaluating, and managing clinical safety information, including serious adverse events (SAEs).
  • Demonstrated ability to contribute to protocol development, clinical study documentation, and cross-functional clinical research activities.
  • Strong organizational, time management, communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams in a global research environment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, and Access.
  • Proficiency in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.

We’re seeking an experienced partner payments operator to manage monthly partner payments for one of our clients, a global tech and media company, supporting its streaming TV business. This is a contract role working with the client’s team.

As an independent vendor, you’ll set the rhythm and own the details. The role suits someone who enjoys making sense of complex agreements, tracking down why numbers don’t match, and building systems that make each month easier than the last.

What you’ll own

  • The monthly close: Calculate what each partner is owed, validate the results, and deliver payment files on time every cycle.
  • Contract-to-calculation logic: Read partner agreements and build the models and rules that turn their terms into accurate payouts.
  • Issue resolution: When something is off, find the source and fix it so it doesn’t come back.
  • Process improvement: Replace manual, error-prone steps with automated workflows.
  • Documentation: Maintain a clear playbook so the process is transparent, auditable, and easy to transfer.
  • Cross-team inputs: Work directly with finance, partnerships, and legal to get what you need.

What success looks like

  • Payments go out accurately and on schedule, month after month
  • Each discrepancy is logged with its cause and fix
  • The playbook stays current and someone new could follow it
  • Manual effort drops measurably over the course of the engagement

How you’ll work

You’ll run the process on your own and check in regularly with the business lead to review progress and resolve open questions (cadence to be agreed). You’ll bring in the client only for decisions that require its approval, such as releasing payments or interpreting ambiguous contract language.

Who we’re looking for

Minimum qualifications

  • Background in partner payments, revenue share, royalty operations, deal desk, or finance operations
  • Ability to read commercial contracts closely and translate their terms into financial logic
  • Advanced SQL and spreadsheet skills
  • Strong attention to detail and comfort working within financial controls
  • Ability to communicate and influence cross-functionally at all levels of management

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in media or streaming, ideally at a large tech or media company
  • Hands-on experience automating workflows or rolling out new tools, including managing the change
  • Experience with partner audits or financial reconciliation
  • Experience working directly with external partners
  • Ability to prioritize and adapt in a fast-paced, evolving environment
