raw.excerpt: About National Council of Urban Indian Health The National Council of Urban Indian Health (NCUIH) was founded to represent the interests of Urban Indian Organizations (UIOs) before Congress and Federal agencies and influence policies impacting the health conditions experienced by urban American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/ANs).
raw.companyName: National Council of Urban Indian Health
raw.description:
About National Council of Urban Indian Health

The National Council of Urban Indian Health (NCUIH) was founded to represent the interests of Urban Indian Organizations (UIOs) before Congress and Federal agencies and influence policies impacting the health conditions experienced by urban American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/ANs). NCUIH is a 501(c)(3), membership-based organization devoted to supporting the development of quality, accessible, and culturally sensitive healthcare programs for AI/ANs living in urban communities. NCUIH provides advocacy, education, training, and leadership for urban Indian healthcare providers and represents UIOs funded through Title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act and the AI/ANs they serve.

Position Summary

The Director of Communications & Events (Director) leads NCUIH's communications function and provides strategic oversight of its annual conference of more than 300 participants and other assigned events. The Director manages staff, leads editorial priorities, digital platforms and communications deliverables across NCUIH's grants and organizational priorities. The Director supervises communications staff and an Events Manager, who is responsible for day-to-day planning and execution of the conference and other NCUIH events. Working under the direction of the Sr. VP of Policy & Communications, the Director sets priorities, delegates responsibilities, monitors budgets and milestones, and ensures communications and events advance NCUIH's mission.

Duties and Responsibilities

Communications leadership and public engagement

  • Develop and maintain an integrated communications and editorial calendar covering grant products, policy priorities, newsletters, organizational announcements, publications, digital content and events.
  • Supervise communications and events staff and coordinate graphic design, website, social media, newsletter, video and podcast production; allocate work and manage external production support.
  • Maintain NCUIH's brand, editorial standards and communications procedures; lead editing and quality review of public-facing materials and route technical, policy and executive approvals.
  • Develop leadership presentations, talking points, speeches, media materials and public relations campaigns assigned by the Sr. VP of Policy & Communications and CEO.
  • Manage press outreach and inquiries as assigned. Manage website and resource-library updates, email marketing and social media.
  • Monitor audience engagement, maintain accurate distribution lists and improve access to NCUIH resources.
  • Maintain professional engagement with national partners, stakeholders, and advocates and foster strong relationships with key national and regional contacts.

Staff supervision and team management

  • Provide direct supervision, coaching and performance feedback to communications staff and the Events Manager; establish clear responsibilities, goals and deadlines.
  • Manage team capacity and coordinate assignments across communications and events; use shared project plans to track deliverables, internal reviews and dependencies.
  • Support staff development and evaluate performance; resolve workload or execution concerns and elevate decisions requiring senior leadership approval.
  • Oversee processes, procedures and workflows of communications and events.

Grant Communications and Dissemination

  • Translate approved workplans into a production schedule with content owners, review deadlines, design needs, publication dates and dissemination measures across new and existing grants.
  • Lead the communications work for the HRSA HIV project, including the design, production, and promotion of HIV webpages, the resource library and learning platform, fact sheets, clinical guides, educational videos, training announcements, and needs-assessment publications, using substantive content developed by program staff and subject matter experts.
  • Coordinate Office of Minority Health (OMH) communications and language-access planning with TARC.
  • Lead the design, production, and promotion of OMH project materials such as prevention materials, the toolkit, UIO snapshots, SME examples, website resources, audio or virtual products and lessons learned materials, using substantive content developed by program staff and subject matter experts.
  • Manage design and dissemination of funded Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) and (Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAI) guidance, training resources and project findings through webpages, newsletters, direct UIO outreach and other approved channels.
  • Working with TARC staff, ensure materials receive appropriate technical and cultural review and meet plain-language and accessibility standards; coordinate translation, captions, transcripts, alternate formats and consent for identifiable stories and media.
  • Lead efforts to compile communications outputs and reach data, including publication records, distribution, webpage use, email engagement, media views and event participation, for grant reporting and improvement.

Conference planning and event implementation

  • Supervise the Events Manager, who is responsible for the integrated event workplan and day-to-day execution of the annual conference and other assigned events, including logistics, vendors, registration, production, accessibility, volunteers and onsite delivery.
  • Set event goals and priorities; review the Event Manager’s workplans, deliverables, milestones, budget tracking and readiness reports, resolve implementation issues and route procurement, contract and financial approvals to Partnerships and Operations.
  • Lead conference marketing, website and agenda publication, speaker materials, signage, attendee communications and the onsite run of show.
  • Coordinate content approval with the CEO, TARC and Policy & Communications, while the Events Manager manages the operational run of show and onsite execution.
  • Ensure the Events Manager partners with the Development Department to execute the conference; integrate fundraising and partnership milestones, sponsor and exhibitor commitments, recognition and fulfillment into the master plan.
  • Lead communications, production and timelines for other assigned webinars, trainings, regional institutes, receptions and convenings.
  • Supervises the Events Manager on operational planning, vendors, platforms, accessibility, logistics and participant follow-up; supervises and assigns tasks to communications staff on promotion and content production.
  • Lead joint planning meetings and post-conference debriefs with the Director of Development and other departments; review results and the Events Manager’s recommendations, coordinate financial reconciliation with the Director of Finance and ensure improvements are implemented.
  • Other communications tasks and events duties as assigned.

Requirements and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, event management or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • At least six (6) years of progressively responsible communications experience, managing complex projects or communications production teams.
  • At least two (2) years' experience directly supervising staff, including assigning work and providing performance feedback.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage editorial planning, digital communications, publications, media relations, and simultaneous deadlines.
  • Experience leading planning and implementation of a complex, multi-day conference or comparable event, including budgets, vendors, cross-functional teams and onsite delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to delegate execution and hold staff accountable for results.
  • Excellent writing, editing, judgment, and quality control skills.
  • Ability to translate public health or policy information for different audiences.
  • Working proficiency with Microsoft 365, project management systems, website content management, email marketing, virtual event tools, and design collaboration tools.
  • Commitment to culturally responsive communication and ability to work respectfully with UIOs and American Indian and Alaska Native communities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree, or equivalent advanced professional experience in communications or a related field.
  • Five or more years' experience managing communications for federally funded grants.
  • Experience in Native health, public health, national associations or nonprofit advocacy, including communications for federal grants.
  • Experience with accessible publication design, video or podcast workflows, media strategy and audience analytics.

NCUIH Team Member Perks

  • Annual Leave: 13 days a year, increases after 3 years, accrued bi-weekly
  • Sick/Safe Leave: 13 days a year, accrued bi-weekly
  • 12 paid holidays a year
  • 100% employer-paid medical premiums for employee and one eligible family member, with a $0 deductible
  • 100% employer-paid dental and vision premiums, including orthodontic coverage
  • Employee Assistance Plan
  • Eligible employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF)
  • 403(b) participation with up to 5% employer match
  • Employer-paid short- and long-term disability
  • Employer-paid life insurance valued at $50,000
  • Optional employee-paid enrollment in AFLAC supplemental benefits

Work/Life Balance and Flexibility are vital to mental, physical, and spiritual health. NCUIH offers the following benefits

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. raw.description:
NikoHealth is a rapidly growing SaaS company transforming how Durable Medical Equipment (DME) and Home Medical Equipment (HME) providers operate. Our innovative, all-in-one platform streamlines business operations, empowering providers to work smarter and more efficiently.

About The Role

This is a newly created role, and one of the first two engineering hires NikoHealth will made in the United States. You'll report directly to the CTO and own how our software gets released and run while working closely with other senior engineers.

We operate dozens of .NET services deployed per-customer on Windows Server and IIS in AWS, managed with Terraform and Octopus Deploy. Across hundreds of provider tenants that's thousands of running application instances. Today a change waits for the next release train, and the train then takes weeks to reach the whole fleet, so end-to-end a given feature takes months. Improving our deployment and development experience is the first job. After that there are dozens of areas of platform investment needed to support how fast we're scaling.

What You'll Do

  • Own our CI/CD pipeline end to end, with the authority to change what it deploys and how.
  • Own developer experience. Reproducible builds, a local environment someone can actually stand up, and fast honest feedback on every change. This is half the job, not a side effect of the other half.
  • Get our automated regression suite running in CI. It exists, it's substantial, and it isn't currently executed.
  • Cut release lead time and get the fleet inside a published, committed release window.
  • Make fleet version state answerable by a query instead of by a person, so anyone can see what a customer is running.
  • Design and publish an access model, so provisioning stops routing through one inbox.
  • Start bringing runtimes and dependencies current, beginning with the shared libraries everything else depends on.
  • Document and share what you learn, so infrastructure knowledge stops being concentrated in one place.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years in platform, infrastructure, or DevOps engineering.
  • Production Terraform, including state you owned and drift you had to reconcile.
  • Production Windows Server and IIS, application pools included.
  • End-to-end ownership of a CI/CD pipeline in a previous role.
  • AWS at the level this estate uses it: EC2, ALB, VPC, IAM.
  • A track record of replacing a manual process with a measured and automated one, where you can tell us the before and after.
  • Evidence you've made other engineers faster, not just the systems. Build times, local setup, test feedback, whatever it was.
  • Daily working use of AI coding agents such as Cursor or Claude Code, including the harness around them: tests, project instructions, and a loop you can run again.

Nice to have

  • Octopus Deploy, or another deployment orchestrator you owned.
  • Single-tenant or multi-tenant SaaS at meaningful scale.
  • Healthcare, HIPAA, or another regulated environment.

How we work

This is brownfield and we're honest about it. Some of this estate is well-built and some of it grew. We're not asking you to rewrite it, because hundreds of providers bill claims through it every day. We're asking you to make it measurable, make it safe to change, then change it. If you've built a career inheriting other people's systems and making them boring, you'll like it here.

We work with AI agents, seriously. The team works agentically and so will you. What matters is what you do after the agent produces something: tests, linters, project instructions, a loop you can run again. If your answer to a bad result is a longer prompt, we're probably not a fit. This is also why developer experience sits in this role rather than somewhere else: an agent is only as good as the feedback loop it runs in, and ours needs work.

Most application development is done by a long-standing engineering partner. You'd own the pipeline, the infrastructure, and the environments, and over time the standards their code meets before it ships while working closely with our off-shore development team.

Two people isn't a platform team, it's the start of one. Until it's three, coverage is shared between you, the CTO, and our head of engineering. Everyone here is remote, and we'd like your hours to overlap the US East Coast.

This is the start of the engineering team, not the end of it. We're hiring more engineers through 2027. The people who join first get the widest scope, the most say in how the team gets built, and first choice about what they own as it grows.

How to apply

Apply through the link on this page. Instead of a cover letter, we ask one question: tell us about a system you inherited, and the first thing you measured. A few sentences is plenty.

Use AI to help write your application if you want to, we do too. We read every one ourselves, and we can tell when nobody read the posting.

Your first conversation will be with our CTO, who is the hiring manager and will walk you through the rest of the process.

Compensation and benefits

  • The range shown for this role is base salary, and does not include equity or bonus. We post it because we expect to pay inside it.
  • Equity in the company.
  • Medical / dental / vision, 401(k) - up to 4% matching, Unlimited PTO policy

This is a remote role, but candidates must be based in the U.S.

  • Review inventory and cost of sales including stock adjustments, COGS checks, and samples
  • Prepare NZ GST returns and AU BAS for review

6. Process Improvement(nice to have)

  • NZ/AU Tax: Understanding of NZ GST, AU GST, and BAS
  • Communication: Clear written English with a habit of asking questions early and escalating when needed

Desirable

  • Interest in automating work and improving processes

raw.description:
About Kreato Global

At Kreato Global, we believe communication is a fundamental human right. Since 2020, Kreato USA Services LLC has provided professional interpreting across healthcare, legal, financial, customer service and community settings. Our services include over-the-phone interpretation (OPI), video remote interpretation (VRI), on-site interpretation and American Sign Language (ASL).

We’re growing our network of remote ASL interpreters who care about accessibility, accuracy and making a real difference in people’s lives.

The role

As a Remote ASL Interpreter, you’ll make communication possible between Deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals and hearing participants over secure video. About 90% of assignments are medical; the other 10% are general community settings.

What you’ll do

  • Interpret ASL ↔ spoken English through our secure VRI platform
  • Facilitate accurate, culturally appropriate communication between Deaf and hard-of-hearing patients, their families and healthcare providers
  • Follow the RID Code of Professional Conduct, standards of practice and applicable regulations
  • Protect patient privacy and comply with HIPAA
  • Stay professional, calm and compassionate, including in sensitive or stressful situations
  • Complete daily activity logs and required documentation accurately and on time

Requirements

  • RID national certification, or another recognized ASL interpreting certification
  • State license or registration, if your state requires one
  • At least 1 year of professional interpreting experience (medical or VRI experience preferred)
  • Strong command of ASL and English, written and spoken
  • Comfortable with video technology and basic troubleshooting
  • Must live in the United States

Remote setup requirements

  • Computer with a webcam and headset
  • Reliable high-speed internet (wired connection preferred)
  • A private, quiet, well-lit workspace where no one else can see or hear sessions
  • A plain, neutral background

You’ll thrive here if you:

  • Pay close attention to detail and own the quality of your work
  • Handle confidential information with discretion
  • Adapt easily to different people, settings and communication needs
  • Work well independently and follow established procedures

Why interpreters work with us

  • Fully remote, on-demand work: you choose when to log in
  • Steady weekday demand in healthcare settings
  • Meaningful work that improves access to care
  • A team that values your expertise and professionalism

How to apply

Apply through JazzHR with your résumé. Include your certifications and, if applicable, your state license. Credentials are verified, and onboarding must be completed before you can receive assignments.

Clinical Research Associate (CRA II or SrCRA) - Oncology - Remote - Bulgaria

At ICON Strategic Solutions, you will work in a sponsor-dedicated model, supported by ICON’s global expertise.


As the world’s largest FSP organisation, with over 90 sponsor partnerships, we offer stability, career development and a collaborative environment where your work contributes to the development of treatments that benefit patients worldwide.


As a Clinical Research Associate at ICON, you will design and analyse clinical trials, interpreting complex medical data, and contribute to the advancement of innovative treatments and therapies.


What You Will Do:

You will contribute to clinical trial monitoring activities, taking responsibility for your deliverables and working collaboratively.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Conducting site qualification, initiation, monitoring, and close-out visits for clinical trials.
  • Ensuring protocol compliance, data integrity, and patient safety throughout the trial process.
  • Collaborating with investigators and site staff to facilitate smooth study conduct.
  • Performing data review and resolution of queries to maintain high-quality clinical data.
  • Contributing to the preparation and review of study documentation, including protocols and clinical study reports

Your Profile:

You will bring relevant clinical trial monitoring experience, along with the following qualifications and skills.

Required qualifications and experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in a scientific or healthcare-related field.
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience as a Clinical Research Associate.
  • In-depth knowledge of clinical trial processes, regulations, and ICH-GCP guidelines.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills, with attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to travel as required (approximately 60%)


Employment with ICON is contingent upon having the legal right to work in the country where the role is based.

Benefits may vary depending on role and location.

ICON is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building an inclusive and accessible workplace where everyone feels valued and supported.
